steps.body: A **rotation** turns a shape around a center point by an angle. Around the origin, a **180° turn** flips both signs: (x, y) → (−x, −y). A point and its 180° image sit on opposite sides of the center.

widget.prompt: Rotate (2, 3) by 180° around the origin. What is the image?

options.feedback: Right — a 180° turn flips both signs: (−2, −3).
That flips only y (a reflection) — a 180° rotation flips BOTH: (−2, −3).
That flips only x — a 180° rotation flips BOTH signs: (−2, −3).
A 180° rotation flips both signs, not swaps coordinates: (−2, −3).

steps.body: A **90° turn counterclockwise** around the origin sends (x, y) → (−y, x): swap the coordinates, then flip the sign of the new first one. For (2, 3): swap to (3, 2), flip the first to get (−3, 2).

explanationVariants: Swap to (1, 4), flip the new first coordinate: (−1, 4).

widget.prompt: Rotate (4, 1) by 90° counterclockwise around the origin. What is the image?

commonEntries.feedback: The rule flips the sign of the new first coordinate: (−1, 4), not (1, 4).
That's a 90° CLOCKWISE turn — counterclockwise gives (−y, x) = (−1, 4).
A 90° CCW turn gives (−y, x) = (−1, 4), not (4, −1).

widget.fallbackFeedback: A 90° counterclockwise turn sends (x, y) → (−y, x).

widget.prompt: Rotate (−5, 2) by 180° around the origin. What is the image?

options.feedback: Right — 180° flips both signs: (−5, 2) → (5, −2).
180° flips BOTH signs — x goes from −5 to 5 as well: (5, −2).
The y also flips: 2 → −2, giving (5, −2).
180° flips both signs, not swaps coordinates: (5, −2).

explanationVariants: (3, 4) → (−3, −4) flips both signs, which is a 180° rotation.
Both signs flipped means a half-turn: 180°.

widget.prompt: A rotation around the origin sends (3, 4) to (−3, −4). What turn was it?

options.feedback: Right — both signs flipped, the signature of a 180° turn.

options.label: 90° counterclockwise
options.feedback: 90° CCW would give (−4, 3) — both signs flipping is 180°.

options.label: 90° clockwise
options.feedback: 90° CW would give (4, −3) — flipping both signs is 180°.
A 360° turn returns the point to (3, 4) unchanged — flipping both signs is 180°.

explanationVariants: A rotation keeps size and shape identical — it only turns the shape's orientation.
Rotations preserve size and shape; they change only the facing direction.

widget.prompt: After a rotation, what is preserved?

options.label: The size and shape — only the orientation turns
options.feedback: Right — a rotation keeps the shape congruent, just turned.

options.label: The size changes
options.feedback: Rotations never resize — the turned shape is exactly the same size.

options.label: The shape gets flipped like a mirror
options.feedback: Flipping is a REFLECTION — a rotation turns without mirroring.

options.label: Nothing is preserved
options.feedback: Size and shape are fully preserved; only the orientation changes.

steps.body: Sort transformations by what they do.
explanationVariants: Slide = translation; flip across a line = reflection; turn around a point = rotation. All three keep size and shape.
Match each action to its transformation name.

widget.prompt: Sort each description by the transformation it names.

items.label: flip across the y-axis
items.feedback: Flipping across a line is a reflection.

items.label: turn 90° around the origin
items.feedback: Turning around a point is a rotation.

items.label: (x, y) → (x − 3, y)
items.feedback: Adding to coordinates is a slide — a translation.

items.label: (x, y) → (x, −y)
items.feedback: Flipping the sign of y across the x-axis is a reflection.

items.label: (x, y) → (−x, −y)
items.feedback: Flipping both signs is a 180° rotation.

widget.missFeedback: Not quite — slide is translation, flip-across-a-line is reflection, turn-around-a-point is rotation.
widget.successFeedback: All sorted — and all three keep the shape the same size and shape.

hints: A slide (adding to coordinates) is a translation.
A flip across a line (one sign flips) is a reflection.
A turn around a point (like both signs flipping) is a rotation.

steps.body: A rotation turns a shape around a center, keeping size and shape.
takeaways: Translations, reflections, and rotations all preserve size and shape.

concept.body: A rotation turns a shape around a center point. Around the origin: 180° sends (x,y)→(−x,−y); 90° counterclockwise sends (x,y)→(−y,x). Size and shape stay the same.

explanationVariants: Rotate (1, 6) by 180°: both signs flip, giving (−1, −6).

widget.prompt: Rotate (1, 6) by 180° around the origin. What is the image?

options.feedback: Right — 180° flips both signs: (−1, −6).
180° flips BOTH signs — x flips too: (−1, −6).
180° flips BOTH signs — y flips too: (−1, −6).
180° flips both signs, not swaps coordinates: (−1, −6).
